item.title: Agentic discovery of interpretable car-following laws from multi-source trajectory data
item.description: Car-following (CF) models is a fundamental component of microscopic traffic simulation and underpin the analysis of collective traffic dynamics, while its modeling becomes more challenging due to diverse human driving behaviors and the increasing presence of automated vehicle. Analytical CF models offer interpretable representations of longitudinal vehicle interactions, but their prescribed functional structures may limit the representation of heterogeneous driving behavior. This study proposes an agent-centered, physics-aware framework for the empirical discovery of CF laws from multi-source — 来源：aws_ml · arxiv — 原文：https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.27836v1

item.title: Noun-verb-conjunction triads [D]
item.description: The neural network would consist of multiple layers with at least one layer consisting of multiple attention heads. Each attention head would hold one triad consisting of one noun + one verb + one conjunction. The siamese cat ate the mouse then died: (Null) Cat ate also Mouse eaten and cat is-siamese Then cat died "Also" means the two events are the same event. (Not in english). A possible conclusion would be "because mouse poisoned" which could then be appended to the input and the process repeated. In addition a few other ideas can be added to each attention head: * the, a, same, this, that, — 来源：arxiv · reddit_ml — 原文：https://www.reddit.com/r/MachineLearning/comments/1xbtzv9/nounverbconjunction_triads_d/

item.title: The Dynamics of Collapse and Recovery in Clustered Federated Learning
item.description: Clustered federated learning (CFL) can suffer from cluster collapse. In particular, under unfavorable initialization, early client assignments concentrate heterogeneous groups on one cluster model, which is then trained toward a pooled compromise, while another model receives no updates. item.title: LocaLeJEPA: Maximum Entropy Representations under Geometric Priors
item.description: Joint-Embedding Predictive Architectures (JEPA) offer an appealing approach to self-supervised learning, but are typically prone to representation collapse. LeJEPA resolves this by introducing a theoretically grounded distribution-matching objective that drives the embedding towards an isotropic Gaussian. However, this approach is fundamentally tied to Euclidean assumptions, and its global target does not reflect domain-specific geometric priors, such as the use of non-Euclidean embedding geometries, e.g., equivariant CNNs or hyperbolic ViTs. item.title: Interruption-Aware Recurrent Reinforcement Learning for UAS Navigation Under Temporary Overrides
item.description: Safe autonomous navigation of UASs requires tactical deconfliction to address conflicts that strategic coordination cannot prevent. This task is challenging under partial observability, when sensor or traffic data are missing, delayed, or degraded. Geometry-based methods can offer separation assurances but face limitations in dense encounters. Recurrent reinforcement learning has therefore been proposed to learn navigation policies that integrate observation-action histories to optimise long-term safety-efficiency trade-offs. item.title: Evolving Agent Interfaces
item.description: Computer-use agents are limited by the interfaces humans give them. An agent may type a spreadsheet cell by cell when a single line of code would do, or print all two thousand lines of a file through a shell to find one function. Both the interfaces and the knowledge of when to use each are built by hand, which cannot keep pace with new applications, workflows, and models. We argue that interface design should itself be an agent capability. We introduce Agent S4, an autonomous computer-use scientist that builds Evolving Agent Interfaces from task experience. item.title: Disclosure Begets Disclosure: A Self-Reinforcing Privacy Loop in LLM Agents with Persistent Memory
item.description: Large language model (LLM) agents increasingly use persistent memory to personalize responses, and personal attributes in this memory pose a privacy risk if exposed. We ask how consulting memory during dialogue changes what users go on to say, and thus what the memory comes to reveal. In multi-session simulations, a simulated user with 24 personal attributes talks with a support agent that does or does not consult memory, and in both settings attributes are inferred from the full accumulated record.
